MINUTES
  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE
  OCTOBER 3, 2023

1.  CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. in the City Hall
  Council Chamber.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Brown Schachter, Combs, Martin, Nash,
  Munday, Persichina, Romanelli, Varner

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Boothe

  ALSO PRESENT:  Sergeant Cervantes, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department
  Deputy Duran, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department

  STAFF PRESENT:  David Wahba, Public Works Director
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Reggie Greene, Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki announced that she is retiring in December. She introduced
Reggie Greene with Willdan who will be taking her place as Traffic Engineering Deputy for the
city.

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES, MAY 17, 2023

COMMITTEE MEMBER PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
VARNER to,

  APPROVE THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  MAY 17, 2023.

There being no objection, CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH/PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST PEDESTRIAN
  CROSSING CONCERNS

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. In March
2023, the City Council directed staff to have a “Turning Vehicles Yield to Pedestrians” sign
installed on Palos Verdes Drive North at Palos Verdes Drive East. The sign was installed on April
22, 2023, and the red curb at that corner was repainted.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that at the last meeting, the committee requested
information on the impact of a “No Right Turn on Red Sign” in this intersection. Traffic counts and
video surveillance were conducted on April 26 and 27, 2023 during the hours of 7:30am – 9:00
am, and 1:00 pm to 1:30 pm. An overview of the data collected was provided with the results of
analysis of the operation of this intersection.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided an explanation of the option for a Leading Pedestrian
Interval which allows for pedestrians to begin going prior to the vehicles. She stated that she does
not believe that this change would impact the overall operation of this intersection.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends that based on the analysis of
provided, it is recommended that the Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI) be implemented at the

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  1
Minutes, October 3, 2023
 intersection of PVD North and PVD East. The assignment of a crossing guard is not
recommended at this time.

In response to a question by CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER, Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki
stated that the time for pedestrians to walk remains the same, but pedestrians “walking man”
begins a few seconds before the light turns green for vehicles.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI, Traffic Engineering Deputy
Itagaki stated the LPI would cause vehicles in all four directions of travel to remain red for a few
seconds in order to give lead time to pedestrians at any given corner.

A brief discussion ensued on how the LPI would work.

John Owens, 19 Hitching Post Drive, provided input on a “No Turn on Red’ sign on Palos Verdes
Drive North at Palos Verdes Drive East, and stated he does not believe that there would be much
impact since the lane clears very easily. Mr. Owens expressed his concerns with this intersection
due to drivers paying attention to vehicular cross-traffic rather than pedestrians. He also
expressed his concern with the amount of signage and visibility at this intersection and provided
photos to compare it with the intersection on Palos Verdes Drive North and Rolling Hills Road,
which has only one sign.

Director Wahba stated that the “No Turn on Red” on Palos Verdes Drive North and Rolling Hills
Road was installed per a request from people who were having issues exiting Peninsula Heritage
School due to the number of vehicles turning right.

A brief discussion ensued on whether to include a timeframe to the “No Turn on Red” sign.

Lynn Yen, 4 Hitching Post Drive, discussed how the walking school bus has been functioning this
school year. She stated that there are about 50 or 60 kids who gather for the walking school bus
and 3 volunteers work together to help the kids’ cross intersections safely. However, one of the
volunteers can only walk the kids across one time. She asked if this initiative could be
encouraged/supported, it could grow to more kids and alleviate traffic.

COMMITTEE MEMBER VARNER asked about the cost for a crossing guard or volunteer crossing
guards.

Deputy Duran stated that he recently responded to an accident where a driver ignored the
crossing guard at Rancho Vista. He stated that there are stipulations in the vehicle code for how
crossing guards are trained and equipped. Having volunteer crossing guards may be a liability
question for the city.

Mrs. Yen stated that crossing guards are not necessarily needed at all four corners; the issue is
at the George F Canyon Nature Center and Dapplegray Park corners. She added that the
superintendent has expressed interest in having a crossing guard at this intersection.

A brief discussion ensued regarding the option of having crossing guards.

Mrs. Yen stated that the pedestrian “walking” signal does not work at the Dapplegray Lanes
School intersection and the crossing guards help move kids across. She expressed concern with
having the LPI and kids being confused with the two intersections.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER stated that she was heartened by the fact that the traffic would
not be negatively impacted by a “no turn on red” sign.

In response to a question by CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER, Deputy Duran stated that about 80%
of people will obey the existing sign.

Director Wahba suggested two signs – one closer to the corner and one across the street, which
would be larger.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
MARTIN to,

Minutes, October 3, 2023
   REMOVE THE EXISTING YIELD SIGNS AND INSTALL TWO “NO TURN ON RED”
  SIGNS WITH NO TIME LIMITS ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AT PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE EAST.

AYES: Brown Schachter, Combs, Martin, Nash, Munday, Persichina, Romanelli, Varner
NOES:
ABSENT: Boothe
ABSTAIN:

Director Wahba stated that this item will be on the City Council agenda for the meeting of Tuesday,
October 10, 2023.

6.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

Director Wahba stated that the city has been awarded a Highway Safety Improvement Grant for
1.5M. The committee has discussed safety issues on Deep Valley Drive, and 250K will be used
for this project. The city is awaiting the completion of the 927 Deep Valley Drive project prior to
beginning this project and repaving the street. Another 250K will be used for Rolling Hills Road
and engineering of that roadway. The last 1M will be used to address all of the guardrails in the
city.

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

COMMITTEE MEMBER MARTIN inquired if the city hired a geotechnical firm for the houses on
Peartree Lane. The city and county have hired Geokinetics and the two homeowners’
associations have hired a company named GMU; the preliminary report by GMU is almost
complete and can be made available to the public by the HOAs.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER stated that she was approached by someone who goes to Ernie
Howlett Park and there are more and more 5k runs are happening there. Vehicles park along
Hawthorne Blvd. above and below the park and when people exit, more space is needed for
visibility. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff can make a work order to have a
portion of the curbs painted red on both sides.

COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS inquired when work would begin on Founders Park. Director
Wahba stated that the city is anticipating that it will begin early next year and that it will be phased,
with landscaping first and the playground equipment installed next fiscal year.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER adjourned the meeting at 7:16 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,  Approved by,

______________________________  _______________________________
